topic: What if you could skip sleep, but the hours went to your shadow?
title: WHAT IF YOU COULD
SKIP SLEEP?

script.text: Midnight. Homework's due. Skip sleep. Done by one.
Three a.m. A whole guitar song. Skip. Nailed it.
Five a.m. Your shadow on the wall... yawns.
What if you could skip sleep?
In 1964, a student stayed awake for eleven days. By day five, he was seeing things. That's real.
So who's yawning on your wall?

science.claim: In 1964 a student stayed awake for eleven days; by day five he was seeing things.
science.working: Randy Gardner, 17, stayed awake 264.4 hours (11 days 25 minutes), ending 8 January 1964. Accounts put his first hallucinations on day four or five; the script says day five.
science.source: Scientific American, How Long Can Humans Stay Awake?; IFLScience; Grunge
